receipts.first_text_witness: You're making $80,000 a year. Decent salary, right? You've been responsible. You've saved some money. You're ready to become a homeowner. So, you open Zillow at midnight on a Tuesday and every single house that doesn't look like it's actively falling apart costs at least $400,000. The kitchen has laminate countertops from 2003. The carpet is that specific shade of beige that screams, "We stopped caring in 1997." There's fake wood paneling in the basement and the listing
receipts.last_text_witness: that it doesn't make sense. Not right now. Not at these prices. Not with your current income. And that's not failure. That's math. That's reality. That's making a decision based on what will actually make your life better instead of what everyone else thinks you should do. Your salary buys you a lot less house than you think it does. And understanding that might be the most valuable financial lesson you learn.
